Hi Maya —

Quick sync re: our badge-scan integration for TechSummit (booth B12). We want to make sure the scan export and consent capture align with HubSpot/SFDC ingestion. High-level asks: 

- Can you confirm the standard badge-scanner export columns you can produce (CSV headers) and whether you can include a last_modified or incremental flag?
- Are you able to provide a nightly consolidated CSV (single file per day) or SFTP incremental files? Which is easier on your side?
- How do you capture consent on the scanner? What field name/value do you include for opt-in to marketing (we need explicit opt-in to pass into HubSpot)?
- We may also send attendees to a QR quick-form; can that payload be joined to the badge export (badge_id or email)?

I attached our desired schema (redwood_lead_schema_v1.csv) — it lists the HubSpot property names we want to populate. Please review and flag any mismatches. 

CC'ing Marissa and Ben to map for HubSpot ingestion and infra. Would love a sample export (first 20 rows) so Ben can validate the mapping. Ideally we can get a test file by EOD Friday, Dec 12.

Thanks — appreciate it.

--

From: Maya Patel <ops@tradeshowco.com>

Subject: Re: Scan-to-CRM consolidation & consent language for TechSummit booth

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear note. We can support the flow you outlined. Quick answers and what I attached: sample_export_head.csv (first 20 rows):

- Export formats: nightly consolidated CSV (preferred) and SFTP incremental files both available. We usually do a consolidated CSV delivered to an S3 bucket or secure SFTP at 11:59 PM local time.
- Columns we include by default: badge_id, first_name, last_name, email, company, title, registration_type, scan_timestamp, device_id, event_id, form_response_id, consent_flag, consent_source. We can add last_modified and a record_id if needed.
- Consent: we capture a boolean consent_flag (TRUE/FALSE) and consent_source (device|qr_form|manual). Consent text is not stored verbatim by default, but we can add a consent_text column if you need it for records.
- QR forms: yes — if you enable the QR form flow, the form_response_id will join to the badge export via badge_id (if attendee scanned) or email if they entered it.

Attached: sample_export_head.csv showing those headers and a few sample rows. We can include an extra consent_text column on request. Let me know if the fields above cover your schema.

Best,
Maya Patel
Event Ops Lead
TradeShowCo
ops@tradeshowco.com

Attachments: sample_export_head.csv (CSV, 2 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <ops@tradeshowco.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 14:35:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Scan-to-CRM consolidation & consent language for TechSummit booth

Thanks, Maya — this is super helpful. Forwarding notes for what Redwood needs to ingest cleanly into HubSpot and SFDC. Attaching a HubSpot mapping worksheet and our updated consent copy for legal.

Mapping notes (proposed):
- badge_id -> custom property: redwood_badge_id
- form_response_id -> redwood_form_id
- scan_timestamp (ISO8601) -> lead.create_date (useful for attribution)
- email -> contact.email (primary dedupe)
- first_name/last_name/company/title -> standard contact properties
- consent_flag -> marketing_opt_in (TRUE/FALSE)
- consent_text -> marketing_consent_text (store verbatim if available)
- device_id/event_id -> meta_event_source

Technical asks / constraints:
- Please include a last_modified column (ISO8601). This allows us to do incremental imports and avoid duplicate creates when someone scans multiple times.
- Dedupe primary key: email if present; fallback to badge_id if email blank.
- Delivery: nightly consolidated CSV to the SFTP path we will provide is preferred. Please name files with eventId_date.csv (e.g., TS2026_20261208.csv).

Consent language: we need the explicit consent_text column if you can capture it at the point of scan or QR form. I've attached consent_text_v2.docx — legal asked for the following phrasing to be associated with the opt-in: 

"I consent to receive marketing communications from Redwood Inference about product updates, events, and offers. I understand my data will be processed according to Redwood's Privacy Policy."

If you cannot capture full consent_text, consent_flag + consent_source + timestamp is acceptable, but please note we prefer verbatim copy stored for compliance records.

Marcus, can you confirm the SFTP destination and user we should expect? We will create the import job on our side once we have a sample file and credentials.

Thanks — attaching: hs_mapping_sheet.xlsx, consent_text_v2.docx, lead_schema.csv. 

--
Ben Carter
Field Ops Lead, Events
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: hs_mapping_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 12 KB); consent_text_v2.docx (DOCX, 3 KB); lead_schema.csv (CSV, 1 KB)
